preconditions: A workflow assumes steps happen in a fixed order or trusts client-supplied values (price, quantity, state) that should be server-authoritative

process.action: Map the full multi-step workflow (cart -> discount -> payment -> confirmation) and note every client-supplied value
process.expected_observation: List of values the client sends that influence the final outcome (price, quantity, currency, state transitions)

process.action: Tamper with server-authoritative-seeming values (price, discount code reuse, negative quantities)
process.expected_observation: Server accepts an inconsistent or attacker-favorable value

process.action: Attempt to skip or reorder workflow steps by calling later-stage endpoints directly
process.expected_observation: Later step succeeds without the required prior step (e.g. payment confirmed without payment)

process.action: Test boundary and negative values (zero/negative price, quantity overflow) for unexpected acceptance
process.expected_observation: Application processes an invalid business value as if valid

impact: Financial loss (free/discounted purchases, negative-price refund abuse)
Workflow bypass leading to unauthorized end states (e.g. order marked shipped without payment)
remediation: Recompute and validate all business-critical values server-side; never trust client-supplied price/quantity/state
Enforce workflow state machines server-side so steps cannot be skipped or reordered
Add server-side sanity bounds on numeric business values
